skill.name: doc-sync-tool
skill.description: Synchronizes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md files across a project so AI agent instructions stay aligned.
skill.summary: Keep shared AI agent instruction files synchronized across a project.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, JavaScript template literals, ANSI color codes, and hardcoded helper commands. Confirmed risks involve local file writes, watch-triggered synchronization, predictable test temporary paths, and unreviewed propagation of AI agent instruction files. No prompt injection attempt, network access, or credential exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Unreviewed overwrites of agent instruction files
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run mode, diff output, explicit confirmation, and automatic backups before writeFileSync updates target files.

remediation.issue: Broad recursive scan and watch scope
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit project root, reject home or filesystem-root targets, and print the exact scope before syncing.

remediation.issue: Rename helpers can modify many files recursively
remediation.suggestion: Add collision checks, dry-run output, and backups, or remove the rename helpers from the published skill.
Use mktemp or fs.mkdtemp for test directories and clean up only paths created by the test process.

remediation.issue: Documentation and implementation use inconsistent filename casing
remediation.suggestion: Update documentation and tests to match uppercase target filenames, or explicitly support both casing styles.

content.value_statement: Teams often maintain separate instruction files for different AI coding tools. This skill synchronizes those files from the newest copy to reduce manual drift.
actual_capabilities: Recursively scans the current working directory for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md files.
Groups matching files by directory and chooses the newest modified file as the source.
Creates missing target files in the same directory when one agent file already exists.
Updates existing target files when their content differs from the newest source file.
Provides a watch mode that resynchronizes files after detected changes.
Includes helper scripts for manual sync, watch mode, renaming, and local tests.
limitations: The sync script overwrites target files without showing a diff or asking for confirmation.
The implementation currently targets uppercase filenames, while some docs mention lowercase variants.
The scanner uses the current working directory and may traverse large project trees.
Watch mode depends on platform support for recursive file watching.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Safe First Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md files. Explain which files would change before running the sync tool.

prompt_templates.title: Check Sync Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the agent instruction files after synchronization. Summarize changed files and highlight any unexpected overwritten content.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Watch Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start watch mode for this project. First identify the project root and explain the directories that will be monitored.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the Sync Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this doc sync workflow. Recommend changes for dry-run support, backups, confirmation prompts, and safer project-root validation.

output_examples.input: Synchronize a project where CLAUDE.md is the newest agent instruction file.
output_examples.output: The tool selects CLAUDE.md as the source and updates AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md in the same folder.

output_examples.input: Start watch mode while editing an agent instruction file.
output_examples.output: The watcher reports the changed file, scans that directory, and synchronizes the matching companion files.

output_examples.input: Validate whether a sync is safe for a repository.
output_examples.output: A reviewer checks the intended source file, confirms expected target files, and verifies the changes with version control.

best_practices: Run the tool only inside a version-controlled project with a clean working tree.
Review the newest source file before syncing because it will overwrite companion files.
Use a narrow project root instead of running from a home directory or shared parent folder.
anti_patterns: Do not run watch mode in a broad directory that contains unrelated projects.
Do not sync after editing untrusted agent instructions without reviewing the content.
Do not rely on the tool as a backup or merge system for divergent documentation.

faq.question: Which files does the sync script target?
faq.answer: The current code targets AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md with uppercase names.

faq.question: How does the tool choose the source file?
faq.answer: It sorts matching files by modification time and uses the newest file as the source.

faq.question: Can the tool overwrite existing content?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes the newest source content into existing target files when content differs.

faq.question: Does it send files to a network service?
faq.answer: No network behavior was found in the reviewed files. The tool operates on local files.

faq.question: Should I use watch mode in production?
faq.answer: Use caution. Watch mode continuously monitors a project root and can overwrite files after changes.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Add dry-run output, backups, confirmation prompts, and consistent filename casing in docs and tests.
